licences.notes: Written out from the printed pages by two independent readers, with a judge settling every difference and a sweep for the marks, then a fresh check until clean; every bar of every part adds up. The Italian translation, the notes printed only for it, and the stage directions are left out. The chorus (offstage at first, on stage from bar 24) is printed on two staves (sopranos and altos, tenors and basses) and is written out as four parts; it is heard with the piano and has no role here. The piano plays the trumpet and timpani lines the print marks “Tromp.” and “Pauk.” (bars 1–2 and 20), as printed. The section begins after the double bar on p. 69 (Allegro maestoso) and ends at the fermata and double bar on p. 71, before Pamina's “Herr! ich bin zwar Verbrecherin!”. Playback tempo: Allegro maestoso ♩ = 98, about 1:48, the median of four complete recordings whose track holds exactly this section (Norrington with the London Classical Players 1:29, Christie 1995 1:47, Haitink 1981 1:49, Böhm 1955 1:52).
